summary: The cache-backed memory path limits performance, rather than DRAM bandwidth or compute throughput.
reasoning: Memory SOL is 71.35% versus 38.7% compute SOL. L2 throughput reaches 75.21% with a 95.62% hit rate, while DRAM throughput is only 16.32%. Long-scoreboard stalls of 61.98% indicate substantial waits for memory dependencies.

root_causes.cause: Global loads use only half of each transferred sector, increasing traffic through the cache hierarchy.

evidence.interpretation: Global-load sector utilization is only 50%, indicating inefficient transaction utilization.
L2 is heavily utilized, making excess cache traffic costly.

fixes.fix: Specialize operand loading and tile layouts for A/B strides so adjacent lanes access contiguous elements along each operand's unit-stride dimension; validate improved sector utilization.
fixes.rationale: Better coalescing reduces sectors transferred per useful byte and relieves pressure on the cache-backed memory path.

root_causes.cause: Insufficient latency hiding leaves warps waiting on operand loads.

evidence.interpretation: Outstanding memory dependencies dominate warp issue stalls.
Moderate occupancy limits the pool of warps available to hide memory latency.
Shared memory imposes a tighter block-residency limit than registers, whose limit is 9 blocks.

fixes.fix: Extend autotuning to jointly sweep num_stages and BLOCK_K, selecting the configuration that reduces long-scoreboard stalls without excessive shared-memory residency loss.
fixes.rationale: Balancing load/compute overlap against resident warps can hide operand-fetch latency more effectively.
